correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\), homogeneity bijects nonalgebraic 1-types with admissible lower/upper pairs. Three exhaustive downset classes yield \(2^{c+1}+f-1\) sigma-invariant downsets. Mixed pairs correspond to disjoint nonempty subsets, giving \(3^c-2^{c+1}+1\) fixed mixed types. Their sum is the stated untwisted character. The order-dual twist fixes the empty pair and nonempty disjoint pairs invariant under sigma²; only alternating halves of even cycles are possible, yielding \(3^e\). Independent all-permutation direct checks (n=2..6, 872 permutations), actual orbit enumeration (n=2..4), and separate Burnside identities agree. Finite tests do not prove the theorem for arbitrary n.

value.rationale: The standard examples are natural extremal posets for Dushnik–Miller dimension. The theorem completely classifies the symmetry action on their one-point extension space, capturing every conjugacy class as well as the order-reversing duality. The parity-only character for duality twists and the quadratic orbit spectrum versus exponential labelled growth give information not recoverable from the previously known scalar counting formula. It is neither an arbitrary numerical slice nor a mere reformulation of a named total.
